hero: India’s services survey strengthened as the Cabinet approved energy-storage and critical-mineral programmes. A new offshore licensing round and altM’s funding put investment execution in focus. The Supreme Court’s detention ruling and CERT-In’s AI audit framework add distinct safeguards for public power and emerging technology.

cards.headline: India's services growth accelerates to 55.8 in October, cost pressures ease to six-year low
cards.brief: S&P Global’s October data put the HSBC India Services PMI at 55.8, up from 55.2 in September, marking the fastest activity expansion in four months. Input cost inflation eased to its lowest level in more than six years.
cards.mechanism: Firmer activity alongside slower cost inflation could give services businesses more room to protect margins.
cards.watch: Watch whether the next survey sustains the improvement in activity and input-cost conditions.

cards.headline: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
cards.brief: The Union Cabinet approved a ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for large-scale energy storage, The Hindu reports. The scheme is designed to support pumped hydro, battery storage and alternative storage technologies.
cards.mechanism: Public funding could help storage projects bridge financing gaps and shift electricity availability toward periods of greater need.
cards.watch: Watch for project awards and financing commitments that turn the approved scheme into buildable storage capacity.

cards.headline: Cabinet approves five-year ₹2,814 cr push for critical mineral processing
cards.brief: The Cabinet approved a five-year ₹2,814 crore scheme for critical-mineral processing, Business Standard reports. Implementation is scheduled from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with the aim of strengthening India’s critical-mineral ecosystem.
cards.mechanism: Support for domestic processing could increase local value addition and reduce exposure to external supply bottlenecks.
cards.watch: Watch for implementation terms and sanctioned projects that establish which processing capacity the programme will actually support.

cards.headline: India opens deepwater oil, gas bids, offers to fund up to 50% of well costs
cards.brief: The government is introducing a special OALP round for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration, with monthly bidding windows and relaxed fiscal terms. It is preparing to cover up to 50% of eligible exploratory well costs under the ₹84,084 crore Samudra Manthan programme; the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons said bid-round details would be announced shortly.
cards.mechanism: Sharing exploration risk could draw investment into costly offshore basins, although discoveries and production would remain uncertain.
cards.watch: Watch the detailed bid notice for eligible costs, fiscal conditions and the acreage available to explorers.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ends distinction between detention and arrest, says 24-hour clock starts when liberty is curtailed
cards.brief: The Supreme Court said the 24-hour clock starts when liberty is curtailed, Hindustan Times reports. Even a person detained for search and seizure must be produced before a magistrate within that period.
cards.mechanism: Counting time from the loss of liberty could limit attempts to delay judicial oversight by postponing a formal arrest label.
cards.watch: Watch how subsequent court orders apply the clock to disputed detention timelines.

cards.headline: Cert-In issues AI security audit guidelines, sets 4-tier risk framework
cards.brief: CERT-In issued AI security audit guidelines with a four-tier risk framework, Hindustan Times reports. It said requirements for high-risk and critical systems apply uniformly, with no exemptions or relaxed standards for smaller firms or startups.
cards.mechanism: Uniform requirements could raise the cost of deploying risky AI systems while reducing gaps in safeguards between large and small providers.
cards.watch: Watch for audit findings that show how firms classify and address high-risk and critical systems.

cards.headline: altM raises $10.3M in Series A funding led by Rainmatter, Mela Ventures
cards.brief: Bengaluru-based altM raised $10.3 million in a Series A round led by Rainmatter and Mela Ventures, YourStory reports. It plans to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, support customer qualification programmes and grow its engineering and commercial teams.
cards.mechanism: Funding production expansion alongside customer qualification could help convert research into repeatable commercial supply.
cards.watch: Watch for manufacturing ramp-up and customer qualification milestones that demonstrate progress beyond the funding announcement.

catalyst_review: Reviewed the complete 392-candidate pool for Friday, November 6. Bosch's explicitly dated November 6 board consideration of a stock split and bonus is a shareholder corporate-action preview without a material policy or operating deliverable, so it does not qualify. Gyftr's results-board alert has no explicit next-day date in the captured summary. SC Agrotech's November 13 meeting, November 12 UP enrolment drive, November 14 Dabur appointment, December 5 DevSparks event and later IPO, digitisation, policy and investment targets fall outside tomorrow. The services release, Cabinet approvals, current cyclone recovery and Wednesday air-quality readings are already reported events rather than next-day catalysts. The deepwater notice promises details shortly but gives no November 6 commitment. No distinct date-specific material catalyst is established.
